input.rationale: Turning the live-cluster statement recorded for the empty-configuration question from source-derived into measured. Every earlier measurement of that question used single-node clusters, so the discriminator asks what happens when the restarted node shares a cluster with a legitimate peer holding the correct configuration. A new focused probe (TestAssurance_LiveClusterEmptyConfigRestart) restarts one follower of a three-voter commit-tracked cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs, then measures (a) what the legitimate leader's continuing heartbeats do to the node's leader view, its configuration and its log, and (b) what one AppendEntries request from a sender that appears in no configuration does to the node, to the serving leader and to the cluster. A local dry run of the same file in the draft work copy produced the events this request expects: the restarted node held an empty configuration with no leader, converged on the serving leader as its heartbeats arrived and stored a command committed after the restart while its configuration stayed empty, and then accepted a higher-term AppendEntries from the sender that is in no configuration, adopted it as leader, raised its term, and the serving leader stepped down with no leader present afterwards. Those local observations are a construction check only; the receipt from this request is the evidence. No interpretation is restated or changed by this update.

scope.description: A three-voter in-memory cluster with a commit-tracking log store and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: the leader applies commands, one follower is shut down and restarted from its own stores on a fresh transport and reconnected, and the probe records the restarted node's recovered configuration and leader, what the legitimate leader's continued heartbeats do to the node's leader view, configuration and log, and what one AppendEntries request from a sender that appears in no configuration, carrying a higher term and no entries, does to the node, to the serving leader and to the cluster.
assumptions: Cluster, transport, log store and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.

Snapshotting is disabled by configuration and the recovered range is small, so the restarted node's configuration is empty rather than stale and NewRaft returns without the FSM batch blocking the parent question covers.
The outsider appears in no configuration the node holds and is wired to the restarted node's transport for the duration of the probe.
Timers are shortened to 200 ms so the observation window stays short.

experiment.prefix: Bootstrap three voters with RestoreCommittedLogs and commit-tracking stores, elect a leader and apply eight commands, shut one follower down and restart it with NewRaft on a fresh in-memory transport, reconnect the cluster, and emit the setup event with the configuration in force and the follower's staged commit index plus the restart-state event with the node's recovered configuration, state, term and leader. Poll until the legitimate leader's heartbeats reach the node, commit one command on the leader, and emit the convergence event with the node's leader, configuration length, state, whether it campaigned, and whether it stored the new command. Then wire a transport for a sender that is in no configuration, send one AppendEntries request with the node's term plus five, no entries and commit index zero, and emit the outsider event with the response, the node's term and leader afterwards, whether the serving leader stepped down and whether the cluster still has a leader.
experiment.requirement: A node that restarts with RestoreCommittedLogs inside a live cluster must not let a server outside the configuration it recovered change its term or its leader in a way that costs the cluster its serving leader.
experiment.responsibility: Raft itself: appendEntries decides whose leadership to record and which term to adopt, and the follower loop decides when the node campaigns from the configuration it recovered.

comparisons.description: The legitimate leader's heartbeats restore the restarted node's leader view.
Heartbeats and replicated entries leave the recovered configuration empty, so only an arriving configuration entry repairs it.
A sender that appears in no configuration does not become the restarted node's leader.
Contact with such a sender does not cost a healthy three-voter cluster its serving leader.

scope.description: Two restart scenarios on a single-node in-memory cluster created by the repository's own MakeClusterCustom helper, whose log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore and whose Config sets RestoreCommittedLogs=true. Each scenario commits entries, restarts the node from its retained log/stable/snapshot stores with a fresh in-memory transport via NewRaft, and reports the recovered commit index, lastApplied, the scan start index, whether a committed configuration entry is inside the scanned range, and the node's latest configuration before and after restart.
assumptions: The CommitTrackingLogStore implementation is the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore.
The transport is the repository's InmemTransport and the FSM is the repository's MockFSM.
RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, as documented in config.go.
No fault injection, no artificial delays and no modification of production logic.

basis.prefix: Scenario A (event restore_committed_logs_no_snapshot): bootstrap a one-node cluster whose first log entry is a committed LogConfiguration, apply ten commands (all committed, no snapshot exists), sample the store's GetCommitIndex and the latest configuration, then Shutdown and restart with NewRaft from the same stores. Scenario B (event restore_committed_logs_snapshot_and_config_change): apply twenty commands, take a user snapshot, commit AddNonvoter(nonvoter-B), apply ten more commands so the commit-tracking store stages a commit index beyond the configuration entry, then Shutdown and restart the same way.
basis.requirement: On restart, a node's configuration state (used for participant eligibility, election gating and quorum) must include every configuration entry its log store reports as committed, including entries at or below the recovered commit index.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: NewRaft owns loading the node's configuration from its log and snapshot history, and the RestoreCommittedLogs option must not leave that state behind the committed history.

scope.description: Two single-node in-memory clusters (repository MakeClusterCustom, CommitTrackingLogStore, RestoreCommittedLogs=true, snapshotting disabled) commit different amounts of authored history, then restart via NewRaft in a goroutine with a bounded wait: 6000 commands as a control (94 batches of 64) and 9000 commands (141 batches). Each case emits a setup event and one result event stating whether NewRaft returned, and, if not, the blocked goroutine frames captured with runtime.Stack.
assumptions: The log store is the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore and the transport the repository's InmemTransport.
Snapshotting is disabled by configuration so the recovered range starts at index 0 with no snapshot.
Only the amount of committed history differs between the two cases; the same harness, helper and configuration are used.
No test is expected to block the whole package run: the restart is wrapped in a bounded select.

basis.prefix: For each case: bootstrap a one-node cluster with CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs, apply N commands to completion, record the staged commit index and the derived batch count, Shutdown, restart with NewRaft from the same stores inside a goroutine and wait up to 20 seconds; on return report lastApplied, commit index and configuration length after restart, otherwise report the observed wait and the frames of every goroutine containing github.com/hashicorp/raft plus chan-send/select markers.
basis.requirement: NewRaft must complete its startup recovery for any legal retained state; RestoreCommittedLogs must not leave the node unable to finish construction when the recovered committed range is large.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: NewRaft owns recovery ordering, including when the FSM consumer goroutine starts relative to the recovery work it feeds.

comparisons.description: The control range (fewer batches than the fsmMutateCh capacity) completes startup recovery.
The range exceeding the fsmMutateCh batch capacity also completes startup recovery.

scope.description: One single-node in-memory cluster (repository MakeClusterCustom, CommitTrackingLogStore, RestoreCommittedLogs=true, snapshotting disabled) commits ten commands, restarts via NewRaft so its configuration is empty, and then receives a RequestVote and a RequestPreVote over a real in-memory transport from a candidate whose ID appears in no configuration. The harness emits one setup event with the log-recorded and live configuration sizes and one result event with the two responses, the derived quorum size and the candidate's membership.
assumptions: The log store is the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore; the candidate transport is the repository's InmemTransport wired to the restarted node's transport.
The candidate's log is up to date and its term is higher than the restarted node's term, so no log-recency or term rule rejects it by itself.
The node's log-recorded configuration (the bootstrapped LogConfiguration at index 1) is the cluster membership in force; the empty live configuration comes from the node's own recovery path.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap a one-node cluster with CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs, apply ten commands, record the log-recorded configuration, Shutdown, restart with NewRaft from the same stores, emit the setup event (log_recorded_config_len, live_config_len, live_voters, derived_quorum_size), then send RequestVote and RequestPreVote through the transport path with candidate ID 'outsider-not-in-log' and emit the responses.
basis.requirement: A node whose configuration is in force (recorded in its own log) must treat vote and pre-vote requests from servers outside that configuration as non-members, and its quorum accounting must follow that configuration.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: the node's configuration state is produced by its own restart recovery, and the admission rules in requestVote/requestPreVote rely on it being populated.

comparisons.description: A candidate that is not in the configuration recorded in the node's log is not granted a vote.

scope.description: One five-voter in-memory cluster with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled. Two voters are removed so the configuration in force is a three-voter set, the node under test snapshots in that state, the two voters are re-added, later traffic is committed, and the node is restarted from its retained stores. Its stub configuration and the peers it replicates to are recorded, leadership is transferred to it, the write it acknowledges is recorded together with the nodes that hold it, every holder is shut down, and the leader elected afterwards is checked for the acknowledged write.
assumptions: Transports are the repository's InmemTransport, log stores the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore, the FSM is the repository's MockFSM, and configuration changes use the public AddVoter/RemoveServer APIs.
ShutdownOnRemove is false so that removing a voter that happens to be the leader does not terminate the process under test.
Only transport-level disconnection is used to isolate a peer; no fault is injected into any node's logic.
The payload check reads each node's log store for the exact byte payload.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap five voters with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs=true; RemoveServer the two voters that will later be re-added; apply a few commands so the FSM can snapshot; take a user snapshot on the node under test while the three-voter configuration is committed; AddVoter both nodes again; apply twenty traffic commands so the node's staged commit index passes the recommitted entries; capture its configuration, shut it down, restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport and rewire the transports; record the live configuration, staged commit index, last applied, and whether the log still holds a configuration entry beyond the snapshot; transfer leadership to the restarted node and wait until it reports Leader; disconnect it from one voter; apply the payload; record each node's possession of the payload, the derived quorums and whether the write was backed by a true majority; shut down every holder; wait for a leader among the survivors and record whether it holds the acknowledged payload.
basis.requirement: An entry that a leader acknowledges to a client must be stored by a majority of the configuration in force at the time, and must be present in the log of any leader later elected from that configuration.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: the leader's commit rule and quorum accounting use the configuration the node recovered, and the node's own recovery path is what leaves that configuration behind the log's committed history.

comparisons.description: The write the stale-configuration leader acknowledges is held by at least a majority of the five-voter configuration in force.

scope.description: A two-voter in-memory cluster applies three commands, commits an AddNonvoter configuration change, and then reports that change's own index, the index from the public configuration future, the documented stats key, and the live configuration, together with the log entry type at the change's index.

The configuration change is committed because its future returned without error, which is the premise for the index comparison.
No internal state is required for the comparison: the change index comes from its public future, the endpoints come from public methods, and the log entry type comes from the log store.

basis.prefix: Start a two-peer cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs and commit-tracking stores; apply five commands; record the follower's configuration and the configuration entry recorded in its log at index 1; shut the follower down and restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport, then rewire all transports; emit the setup event with the configuration before the restart, the log-recorded configuration and the live configuration length after the restart; commit AddNonvoter on the serving leader; wait until the restarted node reports a non-empty configuration and emit the result event with the change index and type and the repaired configuration.

scope.description: A three-voter in-memory cluster with a serving leader: one follower is removed with RemoveServer, the removed node is allowed to receive the entry that drops it from the configuration, and then that removed node sends a TimeoutNow request over the transport to the remaining follower while the leader is healthy. The probe records the configuration in force, the removed node's membership, the target's state and term before and after, the serving leader's state, and who leads afterwards.
assumptions: Cluster, transports and FSM are the repository's own MakeCluster, InmemTransport and MockFSM facilities, and the removal uses the public RemoveServer API.
The removed node stays transport-reachable, which is the situation for a server that has been taken out of the configuration but not shut down.
The request is delivered through the same transport method the library uses for leadership transfer.

basis.prefix: Start a three-voter cluster, wait for a leader and commit one command; choose a follower to remove and another follower as target; RemoveServer the first one and wait until the removed node's own configuration no longer contains it; emit the setup event with the configuration in force, the removed node's membership, the target's state and term, and the leader; send TimeoutNow from the removed node's transport to the target, wait until the target is leader or leadership changes, then emit the result event with the timeout error, the target's state and term, the old leader's state and whether it stepped down, whether a leader is present afterwards and whether the target became it.
basis.requirement: Only the current leader of the configuration in force may trigger a leadership transfer; a server outside that configuration must not be able to make a voter campaign or to displace the serving leader.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: the TimeoutNow handler decides what a received transfer trigger means, and the vote handler decides how much trust to extend to a transfer-flagged campaign.

comparisons.description: A server outside the configuration in force cannot change who leads.
The serving leader keeps its authority when a non-member sends a transfer trigger.

scope.description: A single-node in-memory cluster with a commit-tracking store and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled is restarted from its own stores so its configuration is empty; the node is then watched over several heartbeat timeouts for any campaign of its own, after which an outsider reachable through the transport sends one AppendEntries request with a higher term and no entries, and the node's state, its leader identity and the response are recorded.

basis.requirement: A node that recovers its configuration from its own log must not store or apply entries sent by a server outside that configuration.

scope.description: A four-peer in-memory cluster with slowed timers is reduced to three voters plus one non-voter by demoting one follower; the leader is then disconnected from the two remaining voters in both directions while the non-voter stays wired, reachability is tested directly, and VerifyLeader is called with a bounded wait.
assumptions: Cluster, transports and FSM are the repository's own MakeCluster, InmemTransport and MockFSM facilities; the demotion uses the public DemoteVoter API.
Timers are slowed for the probe so the leader lease does not step the leader down before the verification completes; the lease itself counts only voters.
Isolation is transport-level disconnection in both directions, and reachability is confirmed by direct AppendEntries attempts from the leader's transport.

basis.prefix: Start a four-peer cluster with one-second heartbeat and lease timers; wait for a leader and apply one command; DemoteVoter a follower so the configuration is three voters plus one non-voter; disconnect the leader from the other two voters in both directions; attempt one AppendEntries to the non-voter and one to a voter and record the errors; emit the setup event with the voters, the voter quorum, the two reachability results and the two node identifiers; call VerifyLeader in a goroutine with a five-second bound and emit the result event with whether it returned, its error, whether it succeeded, the elapsed time and the leader's state afterwards.
basis.requirement: Leader verification must not report success unless a quorum of the voters of the configuration in force has acknowledged, so that a client cannot take the result as evidence that the node still leads the cluster.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: verifyLeader chooses which peers' acknowledgements count and the replication map it uses is built by the library.

comparisons.description: A server outside the configuration in force cannot change who leads.
The serving leader keeps its authority when a non-member sends a transfer trigger.

scope.description: A single-node in-memory cluster with a commit-tracking store and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled is restarted from its own stores so its configuration is empty; the node is then watched over several heartbeat timeouts for any campaign of its own, after which an outsider reachable through the transport sends one AppendEntries request with a higher term and no entries, and the node's state, its leader identity and the response are recorded.
assumptions: Cluster, transport, log store and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.
Snapshotting is disabled by configuration so the restarted node's configuration is empty rather than stale.
The outsider is a server that appears in no configuration the node holds; it is wired to the node's transport for the duration of the probe.
The AppendEntries request carries no entries, so accepting it only means accepting the sender as leader.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap a one-node cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs and commit-tracking stores, apply five commands, shut the node down, restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport and emit the setup event with the live configuration length and whether the node is in its own configuration; sleep six heartbeat timeouts and record the node's state and any leader it knows; wire an outsider transport, send AppendEntries from the outsider with term+1, no entries and commit index 0, then emit the result event with the response success, the response term, the leader the node now reports and whether the outsider became that leader.
basis.requirement: A node that recovers from its own log must not accept a server outside the configuration it recorded as its leader, and its own election gating must stay consistent with the configuration it holds.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: appendEntries decides whose leadership to record and the follower loop decides when the node campaigns, both from the configuration the node recovered.

comparisons.description: A server outside the node's configuration does not become the node's leader.
The node does not start an election of its own while its configuration is empty.

scope.description: The same single-node empty-configuration restart as the previous case, extended by one phase: after the outsider is accepted as leader, it sends one AppendEntries carrying a single command entry with a commit index covering it, and the probe records whether the entry is stored in the node's log and reaches its FSM.
assumptions: Cluster, transport, log store and FSM are the repository's own test facilities; snapshotting is disabled so the configuration is empty.
The outsider remains transport-reachable and its term is the node's current term at the time of the second request.
The entry is a plain command entry with no configuration semantics.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap a one-node cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs and commit-tracking stores, apply five commands, restart the node with NewRaft on a fresh transport and emit the setup event; sleep six heartbeat timeouts and record state; send an outsider AppendEntries with term+1 and no entries, then send a second AppendEntries from the same outsider carrying one command entry with a leader commit index covering it; wait for the applied index to advance, scan the log store for the payload, and emit the outsider-entries event with the stored flag, the last index and the last applied index before and after.
basis.requirement: A node that recovers its configuration from its own log must not store or apply entries sent by a server outside that configuration.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: appendEntries decides whose requests are processed and processLogs decides what reaches the FSM.

comparisons.description: An entry sent by a server outside the recovered configuration neither is stored nor reaches the FSM.

scope.description: A four-peer in-memory cluster with slowed timers is reduced to three voters plus one non-voter by demoting one follower; the leader is then disconnected from the two remaining voters in both directions while the non-voter stays wired, reachability is tested directly, and VerifyLeader is called with a bounded wait.
assumptions: Cluster, transports and FSM are the repository's own MakeCluster, InmemTransport and MockFSM facilities; the demotion uses the public DemoteVoter API.
Timers are slowed for the probe so the leader lease does not step the leader down before the verification completes; the lease itself counts only voters.
Isolation is transport-level disconnection in both directions, and reachability is confirmed by direct AppendEntries attempts from the leader's transport.

basis.prefix: Start a four-peer cluster with one-second heartbeat and lease timers; wait for a leader and apply one command; DemoteVoter a follower so the configuration is three voters plus one non-voter; disconnect the leader from the other two voters in both directions; attempt one AppendEntries to the non-voter and one to a voter and record the errors; emit the setup event with the voters, the voter quorum, the two reachability results and the two node identifiers; call VerifyLeader in a goroutine with a five-second bound and emit the result event with whether it returned, its error, whether it succeeded, the elapsed time and the leader's state afterwards.
basis.requirement: Leader verification must not report success unless a quorum of the voters of the configuration in force has acknowledged, so that a client cannot take the result as evidence that the node still leads the cluster.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: verifyLeader chooses which peers' acknowledgements count and the replication map it uses is built by the library.

comparisons.description: Verification fails while only a non-voter can acknowledge.

scope.description: A five-peer in-memory cluster with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled is reduced to three voters, one node snapshots in that state, the two removed voters are re-added and traffic is committed, and that node is restarted from its stores so its recovered configuration is the three-voter set. Two vote requests are then delivered over the transport from different candidates, identical except for identity and both flagged as leadership transfers.
assumptions: Cluster, transports, log stores and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.
The candidates' requests carry a higher term and an up-to-date log so that only the membership rule and, for the control, the remaining checks decide the outcome.
Both requests set the leadership-transfer flag, which the vote handler uses to skip its leader-availability rejection, so the comparison isolates the membership rule.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap five voters with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs=true; RemoveServer the two voters that will be re-added; apply pre-snapshot commands; snapshot the node under test while the three-voter configuration is committed; AddVoter both nodes again; apply twenty traffic commands so the node's staged commit index passes those entries; capture its configuration, shut it down, restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport and rewire the transports; emit a setup event with the recovered and in-force voter sets and the two candidate identities, then send two RequestVote messages over the transport, one from the re-added voter (outside the recovered set) and one from a voter inside it, both with a higher term, an up-to-date log and the leadership-transfer flag set; emit the event with both results, the recovered and in-force voter sets, and whether each candidate is a member of the configuration in force.
basis.requirement: A node must treat a server that the configuration in force lists as a voter as an eligible participant, so that elections can still gather a majority of the configuration in force.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: requestVote decides membership from the configuration the node recovered, and the recovery path is what leaves that configuration behind the log's committed history.

comparisons.description: A voter of the configuration in force that is outside the recovered set is not rejected while the control candidate inside the recovered set is granted.

scope.description: A three-voter in-memory cluster with commit-tracking stores, RestoreCommittedLogs, a low snapshot threshold and small trailing-log retention: one node snapshots, a configuration change adds a non-voter, traffic advances the node's staged commit index past that entry, the node is shut down, the cluster commits eighty more entries while that node is gone, and the node is then restarted from its stores. The probe records the recovered configuration, the node's snapshot index and the leader's snapshot index before the wait, then waits for the configuration in force to be restored and records the resulting configuration, snapshot index and last log index.
assumptions: Cluster, transports, log stores and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.
The node's shutdown and restart are the ordinary public operations used elsewhere in this harness; no bytes are removed or altered.
The leader's log is expected to have been compacted past the restarted node's next index, which is what makes an installed snapshot the only way to catch the node up.

basis.prefix: Start a three-peer cluster with commit-tracking stores, RestoreCommittedLogs and snapshot threshold twenty with trailing logs five; apply ten commands; snapshot the node under test; commit AddNonvoter for a late joiner; apply five more commands so the node's staged commit index passes that entry; record its last log index and shut it down; apply eighty more commands on the leader so it snapshots and compacts; restart the node with NewRaft on a fresh transport and rewire; emit the setup event with the configuration in force, whether the late joiner is in it, whether the recovered configuration has it, the recovered length, the recorded last log index, the node's snapshot index after restart and the leader's latest snapshot index; wait, bounded by twenty seconds, for the late joiner to appear in the node's configuration and emit the result event with the repaired flag, the configuration after the wait and the snapshot and last log indexes after the wait.
basis.requirement: A node whose recovered configuration is behind the configuration in force must regain the configuration in force when the leader can only catch it up with an installed snapshot.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: the node's configuration is loaded by its own recovery and updated by the snapshots and entries it receives.

comparisons.description: The node regains the configuration in force after the leader catches it up.
The restoration arrives with an installed snapshot, which the node's snapshot index shows.

scope.description: A single-node history is written directly into a commit-tracking store that also reports itself as monotonic: a configuration entry at index 1, ten command entries above it, and a staged commit index covering them, with the stable store holding term one. NewRaft is then run against that store with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and snapshotting disabled, and the probe reports the store's monotonicity, the last log index, the staged commit index, the applied index, and the node's configuration after construction.
assumptions: The store is the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore wrapped by a harness type whose IsMonotonic reports true; the stable store, transport, FSM and snapshot store are the repository's own in-memory facilities.
The history is the same one a bootstrapped single-node cluster writes: a configuration entry at index 1 followed by commands, with the commit index staged as the entries are stored.
No snapshot exists, so the recovered configuration can only come from the scan or from nothing.

basis.prefix: Create the monotonic commit-tracking store and an in-memory stable store; store a configuration entry at index 1 for a single voter named self, then ten command entries at indexes 2 to 11; stage commit index eleven; set the stable store's current term to one; build a DefaultConfig with LocalID self, RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, a very large snapshot threshold and a one-hour snapshot interval; construct the node with NewRaft over an in-memory transport and snapshot store; emit the resulting store monotonicity, last log index, staged commit index, applied index and the node's configuration.
basis.requirement: A node constructed from a store that reports a configuration entry as committed must hold the configuration that entry records, whatever shape the store has.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: NewRaft decides how the recovered configuration is established, independently of the store implementation.

scope.description: A five-peer in-memory cluster with commit-tracking stores, RestoreCommittedLogs and snapshotting disabled by configuration: two voters are removed, both are re-added, fifteen commands are committed, the node under test snapshots in that state, and it is then restarted from its stores. The probe reports the snapshot's index and configuration size, the configuration in force, the recovered configuration size and whether the two match.
assumptions: Cluster, transports, log stores and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.
The snapshot is taken while the widened configuration is committed, so the snapshot records the configuration in force.
No bytes are altered outside the public snapshot, removal, addition and restart operations.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap five voters with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs=true; RemoveServer two voters and AddVoter them again through the retrying helper; apply fifteen commands; take a user snapshot on the node under test and record its index and configuration size together with the configuration in force; shut the node down and restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport; emit the event with the snapshot index, both configuration sizes, whether the recovered configuration matches the configuration in force and whether the gap is absent.
basis.requirement: A node whose snapshot already covers a configuration change must recover the configuration in force on restart, whatever lies in its log below the commit index it recovers.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: NewRaft establishes the recovered configuration from the snapshot and the log, and this probe names the boundary of the condition under which it fails.

scope.description: A three-voter in-memory cluster is started, one follower is removed through the public API and stays transport-reachable, and then three rounds follow: each round sends a TimeoutNow request from the removed node's own transport to a surviving follower that is not the current leader, waits for the leadership to change, and records how many rounds changed leadership, how many ended with a leader present, and the target's term after each round.
assumptions: Cluster, transports and FSM are the repository's own MakeCluster, InmemTransport and MockFSM facilities; the removal uses RemoveServer.
The removed node keeps its transport routes, which is the situation of a server taken out of the configuration but not shut down.
Timers are shortened so each round settles quickly; the request is sent from the removed node's own transport, which already routes to every peer.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap a three-voter cluster with shortened election, heartbeat and lease timers; wait for a leader and apply one command; choose a follower, RemoveServer it and wait until its own configuration no longer contains it; then for three rounds pick a surviving follower other than the current leader, record the current leader and the target's term, send TimeoutNow from the removed node's transport to the target, wait up to five seconds for the leadership to change, and count the rounds that changed leadership and the rounds that ended with a leader; finally emit the counts, whether churn persisted over at least two rounds and the term recorded after each round.
basis.requirement: A cluster must not let a server outside the configuration in force repeatedly displace its leader: leadership changes must not be triggerable round after round by the same non-member sender.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: the TimeoutNow handler decides what a received transfer trigger means, and the vote handler decides how much trust to extend to a transfer-flagged campaign.

scope.description: A three-voter in-memory cluster with a commit-tracking log store and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: the leader applies commands, one follower is shut down and restarted from its own stores on a fresh transport and reconnected, and the probe records the restarted node's recovered configuration and leader, what the legitimate leader's continued heartbeats do to the node's leader view, configuration and log, and what one AppendEntries request from a sender that appears in no configuration, carrying a higher term and no entries, does to the node, to the serving leader and to the cluster.
assumptions: Cluster, transport, log store and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.

Snapshotting is disabled by configuration and the recovered range is small, so the restarted node's configuration is empty rather than stale and NewRaft returns without the FSM batch blocking the parent question covers.
The outsider appears in no configuration the node holds and is wired to the restarted node's transport for the duration of the probe.
Timers are shortened to 200 ms so the observation window stays short.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap three voters with RestoreCommittedLogs and commit-tracking stores, elect a leader and apply eight commands, shut one follower down and restart it with NewRaft on a fresh in-memory transport, reconnect the cluster, and emit the setup event with the configuration in force and the follower's staged commit index plus the restart-state event with the node's recovered configuration, state, term and leader. Poll until the legitimate leader's heartbeats reach the node, commit one command on the leader, and emit the convergence event with the node's leader, configuration length, state, whether it campaigned, and whether it stored the new command. Then wire a transport for a sender that is in no configuration, send one AppendEntries request with the node's term plus five, no entries and commit index zero, and emit the outsider event with the response, the node's term and leader afterwards, whether the serving leader stepped down and whether the cluster still has a leader.
basis.requirement: A node that restarts with RestoreCommittedLogs inside a live cluster must not let a server outside the configuration it recovered change its term or its leader in a way that costs the cluster its serving leader.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: appendEntries decides whose leadership to record and which term to adopt, and the follower loop decides when the node campaigns from the configuration it recovered.

comparisons.description: The legitimate leader's heartbeats restore the restarted node's leader view.
Heartbeats and replicated entries leave the recovered configuration empty, so only an arriving configuration entry repairs it.
A sender that appears in no configuration does not become the restarted node's leader.
Contact with such a sender does not cost a healthy three-voter cluster its serving leader.
